rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition of a wife's mother includes her original mother and all grandmothers through either parent, as with lineage generally.
rows.anchor: الأمهات الأصلية وجميع جداتها من قبل الأب والأم كما بينا مثله في النسب

rows.speaker: الأكثرين من الصحابة والتابعين
rows.claim: The majority of Companions and Successors hold that marrying a woman prohibits her mother whether or not the marriage is consummated.
rows.anchor: مذهب الأكثرين من الصحابة والتابعين أن من تزوج بامرأة حرمت عليه أمها سواء دخل بها أو لم يدخل

rows.speaker: علي وزيد وابن عمر وابن الزبير وجابر وابن عباس
rows.claim: A group of Companions, including Ali, Zayd, Ibn Umar, Ibn al-Zubayr, Jabir, and according to the strongest reports Ibn Abbas, hold that the mother is forbidden only after intercourse with the daughter, like a stepdaughter.
rows.anchor: وهو قول علي وزيد وابن عمر وابن الزبير وجابر ، وأظهر الروايات عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: جمع من الصحابة
rows.claim: Their grammatical argument is that the verse states two rulings and then one condition, so the condition applies to both rulings.
rows.anchor: ذكر حكمين وهو قوله : { وأمهات نسائكم وربائبكم اللاتى فى حجوركم } ثم ذكر شرطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors the majority: 'your wives' mothers' is an independent clause, and no proof makes the later condition govern it.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { وأمهات نسائكم } جملة مستقلة بنفسها ولم يدل الدليل على عود ذلك الشرط اليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A condition must attach to something already stated; attaching it to one clause suffices, while extending it to the other abandons the apparent wording without proof.
rows.anchor: الشرط لا بد من تعليقه بشيء سبق ذكره فاذا علقناه باحدى الجملتين لم يكن بنا حاجة إلى تعليقه بالجملة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause's general meaning is certain, whereas the condition's return to it is only a possibility; restricting the generality on that uncertain basis is impermissible.
rows.anchor: عموم هذه الجملة معلوم ، وعود الشرط اليه محتمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the condition applies only to mothers-in-law, stepdaughters would be forbidden without consummation, which consensus rejects.
rows.anchor: يلزم القول بتحريم الربائب مطلقا ، وذلك باطل بالاجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it applies to both clauses, 'min' would have to mean 'from among' for mothers-in-law and origin for stepdaughters, improperly giving one word two senses.
rows.anchor: فيلزم استعمال اللفظ الواحد المشترك في كلا مفهوميه وانه غير جائز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible reply is that 'min' means connection in both clauses, as in the verse describing believing men and women as allies of one another.
rows.anchor: إن كلمة ( من ) للاتصال كقوله تعالى : { والمؤمنون والمؤمنات بعضهم أولياء بعض }

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Amr ibn Shuayb, from his father, from his grandfather, says a man may not marry his wife's mother whether or not he consummated the marriage; if he married the mother and divorced her before consummation, he may marry the daughter. Al-Tabari challenged its authenticity.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه عن جده عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : اذا نكح الرجل المرأة فلا يحل له أن يتزوج أمها

rows.speaker: محمد بن جرير الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari criticized the authenticity of the report about marrying a wife's mother.
rows.anchor: وطعن محمد بن جرير الطبري في صحة هذا الحديث

rows.speaker: عبدالله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud once permitted marrying a woman's mother after divorcing her before intercourse; after seeing the people of Medina united against his ruling, he returned to Kufa and ordered a man to leave that wife.
rows.anchor: وكان عبدالله بن مسعود يفتي بنكاح أم المرأة اذا طلق بنتها قبل المسيس

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit says that after divorce before consummation a man may marry his wife's mother, but after her death he may not.
rows.anchor: روى قتادة عن سعيد بن المسيب أن زيد بن ثابت قال : الرجل اذا طلق امرأته قبل الدخول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains that divorce before consummation carries no rulings of consummation, including no waiting period, while death counts like consummation for the waiting-period rule and therefore triggers this prohibition.
rows.anchor: الطلاق قبل الدخول لا يتعلق به شيء من أحكام الدخول ، ألا ترى أنه لا يجب عليها عدة ، وأما الموت فلما كان في حكم الدخول في باب وجوب العدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A stepdaughter (rabiba) is a man's wife's daughter by another man; the word means one brought up because the man raises her, and the two cited verbs have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: الربائب : جمع ربيبة ، وهي بنت امرأة الرجل من غيره ، ومعناها مربوبة

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit records two case-vowel pronunciations for حجر, with fatḥ or kasr.
rows.anchor: قال ابن السكيت : حجر الانسان وحجره بالفتح والكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'In your care' means in your upbringing; it is a metaphor because a person raising a child seats the child in his lap, like saying she is in someone's custody, whose root is the armpit or bosom.
rows.anchor: والمراد بقوله : { فى حجوركم } أي في تربيتكم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda interprets 'in your care' as being in your homes.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة : في حجوركم أي في بيوتكم

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali permitted marrying a stepdaughter living elsewhere and outside the husband's care after he had consummated marriage with her mother, reasoning that being in his care is a condition of the prohibition.
rows.anchor: روى مالك بن أوس بن الحدثان عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه قال : الربيبة اذا لم تكن في حجر الزوج

rows.speaker: سائر العلماء
rows.claim: Other scholars hold that consummation with the mother forbids her daughter whether or not she was raised by the husband, because the verse makes absence of consummation the basis for there being no blame.
rows.anchor: وأما سائر العلماء فانهم قالوا : إذا دخل بالمرأة حرمت عليه ابنتها سواء كانت في تربيته أو لم تكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects care as a legal condition: the verse mentions the usual case, since a wife's daughter is ordinarily raised by her husband.
rows.anchor: هذا الكلام على الأعم ، لا أن هذا القيد شرط في حصول هذا التحريم

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Razi argues that adultery creates affinity prohibitions: 'entering' a woman means intercourse whether lawful or illicit, so adultery with a mother forbids her daughter.
rows.anchor: تمسك أبو بكر الرازي في إثبات أن الزنا يوجب حرمة المصاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls this argument extremely weak because the verse concerns a woman who was already one of the man's wives before intercourse, a status an adulteress lacks.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاستدلال في نهاية الضعف ، وذلك لأن هذه الآية مختصة بالمنكوحة لدليلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording 'from your women whom you entered' implies that being one of his women precedes intercourse; the verse also divides his women into those entered and not entered, so the two statuses differ.
rows.anchor: قوله : { من نسائكم اللاتى دخلتم بهن } يقتضي أن كونها من نسائه يكون متقدما على دخوله بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marriage makes a woman one of a man's wives by contract before intercourse, but adultery creates no prior status that makes her one of his women.
rows.anchor: في النكاح صارت المرأة بحكم العقد من نسائه سواء دخل بها أو لم يدخل بها ، أما في الزنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An adulteress is likewise excluded from a bequest to a man's wives and from a legally binding oath about a family's wives, reinforcing that she is not included in the wording.
rows.anchor: لو أوصى لنساء فلان ، لا تدخل هذه الزانية فيهن ، وكذلك لو حلف على نساء بني فلان

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafii prohibits a father from marrying his son's slave woman, whereas Abu Hanifa permits it.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي رحمه الله : لا يجوز للأب أن يتزوج بجارية ابنه ، وقال أبو حنيفة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafii's argument is that the son's slave woman is his halila, and the verse prohibits a son's halila to his father.
rows.anchor: جارية الابن حليلة ، وحليلة الابن محرمة على الأب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author derives halila from permissibility, making it a woman made lawful, and from hulul, making it a place where the master resides; both cover a slave woman.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أن يكون مأخوذا من الحل الذي هو الاباحة ، فالحليلة تكون بمعنى المحلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author gives two further derivations: the pair is as if settled together in one garment, cover, or home, or each settled in the other's heart and spirit through love and intimacy.
rows.anchor: لشدة اتصال كل واحد منهما بالآخر كأنهما يحلان في ثوب واحد وفي لحاف واحد وفي منزل واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conventional phrase 'a man's halila' meaning his wife does not exclude a slave woman; defining the word broadly to include both defeats the contrary linguistic claim, which is only negative testimony.
rows.anchor: إنا لا ننكر أن لفظ الحليلة يتناول الزوجة ، ولكنا نفسره بمعنى يتناول الزوجة والجارية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'From your loins' excludes an adopted son: early Islam treated an adopted child as a son, but the wife of a man merely claimed as a son is not forbidden if he is not his biological son.
rows.anchor: قوله : { الذين من أصلابكم } احترازا عن المتبني ، وكان المتبني في صدر الاسلام بمنزلة الابن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Zayd ibn Haritha divorced Zaynab bint Jahsh, the Prophet married her; the polytheists accused him of marrying his son's wife, and the cited verses denied that adoption makes adopted sons true sons and removed blame from marrying their former wives.
rows.anchor: نكح الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم زينب بنت جحش الأسدية وهي بنت أميمة بنت عبد المطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent wording excludes a milk-son's wife, while 'what is beyond these' in the next verse appears to permit her; the Prophetic rule that nursing forbids what lineage forbids specifies that general permission, so a solitary report narrows the Qur'an's general wording.
rows.anchor: ظاهر قوله : { وحلائل أبنائكم الذين من أصلابكم } لا يتناول حلائل الأبناء من الرضاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree that a son's wife becomes forbidden to his father as soon as the marriage contract is made, whether or not the son consummated it, because the verse is general.
rows.anchor: اتفقوا على أن حرمة التزوج بحليلة الابن تحصل بنفس العقد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says to leave unspecified the condition God left unspecified; here that means the prohibition is permanent, not that the ruling is obscure, as with the seven permanently forbidden blood relations called the unspecified ones.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس : أبهموا ما أبهمه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition also covers a grandson's wife; this shows that a grandson is called one of the grandfather's loins and is descended from him.
rows.anchor: اتفقوا على أن هذه الآية تقتضي تحريم حليلة ولد الولد على الجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'and combining two sisters' is grammatically nominative, with an implied sense: forbidden to you are your mothers, daughters, and combining two sisters.
rows.anchor: قوله : { وأن تجمعوا بين الاختين } في محل الرفع ، لأن التقدير : حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم وبناتكم والجمع بين الأختين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Combining two sisters occurs through marrying both, owning both, or marrying one while owning the other; simultaneous marriage to both raises the possible rulings of upholding the union, choosing one, allowing later choice, or voiding it.
rows.anchor: الجمع بين الأختين يقع على ثلاثة أوجه : إما أن ينكحهما معا ، أو يملكهما معا ، أو ينكح إحداهما ويمكل الاخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The simultaneous marriage is void under the verse; this challenges Abu Hanifa's principle that prohibition does not entail invalidity, illustrated by prohibited triple divorce, exchanging one dirham for two, and other corrupt sales.
rows.anchor: أما الجمع فباطل بحكم هذه الآية هكذا قالوا ، إلا أنه مشكل على أصل أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although someone might compare this to prohibited divorce during menstruation or a post-menstrual purity in which intercourse occurred, the author says a subtle distinction between the cases is explained in his work on disputed issues.
rows.anchor: قلنا : بين الصورتين فرق دقيق لطيف ذكرناه في الخلافيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Voiding both contracts is the remaining sound outcome: choosing one lacks a differentiating basis, and leaving the choice until later presupposes a valid continuing contract.
rows.anchor: وأما أن التعيين أيضا باطل ، فلأن الترجيح من غير مرجح باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a man marries one sister and then the other, the second marriage is void because preventing a new prohibition is easier than undoing an established one.
rows.anchor: فههنا يحكم ببطلان نكاح الثانية ، لأن الدفع أسهل من الرفع

rows.speaker: علي وعمر وابن مسعود وزيد بن ثابت وابن عمر
rows.claim: Ali, Umar, Ibn Masud, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Ibn Umar prohibit combining two sisters through ownership, or by marriage to one and ownership of the other; other Companions permit it.
rows.anchor: فقد اختلفت الصحابة فيه ، فقال علي وعمر وابن مسعود وزيد بن ثابت وابن عمر : لا يجوز الجمع بينهما

rows.speaker: علي وعمر وابن مسعود وزيد بن ثابت وابن عمر
rows.claim: The prohibiting group argues that the verse's apparent generality forbids combining sisters in every form.
rows.anchor: ظاهر الآية يقتضي تحريم الجمع بين الأختين مطلقا

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: Uthman says one verse permits the pairing and another forbids it, and that permission takes priority; he cites the exception for those owned by the right hand and a similar exception for spouses or those owned.
rows.anchor: وعن عثمان أنه قال : أحلتهما آية وحرمتهما آية ، والتحليل أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited permissions do not permit combining the sisters even in intercourse: Muslims agree intercourse with both is forbidden, and if ownership of both permitted intercourse by the cited rule, it would be permitted, which it is not.
rows.anchor: أن المسلمين أجمعوا على أنه لا يجوز الجمع بين الأختين في حل الوطء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The author reports the Prophetic rule that when the forbidden and permitted meet, the forbidden prevails, supporting the prohibition of combining them in ownership.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( ما اجتمع الحرام والحلال إلا وغلب الحرام الحلال )

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The author also invokes the Prophetic advice to leave what causes doubt for what does not.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( دع ما يريبك إلى ما لا يريبك )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ali's position is favored by caution: sexual relations are presumptively forbidden, and when evidence about a contract's conditions is balanced, prohibition is required; the lawfulness of marriage is an exception to that baseline.
rows.anchor: مبنى الابضاع في الأصل على الحرمة ، بدليل أنه إذا استوت الامارات في حصول العقد مع شرائطه وفي عدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reasons that if sexual relations lacked humiliation and harm, marriage to mothers would be lawful because serving them benefits them; its prohibition shows the practice entails harm, so prohibition is the baseline and lawfulness an exception.
rows.anchor: لو كان خاليا عن جهة الاذلال والضرر ، لوجب أن يكون مشروعا في حق الأمهات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under the better-known juristic view, a man may own two enslaved sisters, but intercourse with one makes the other forbidden until he relinquishes ownership of the first by sale, gift, emancipation, manumission contract, or marriage.
rows.anchor: وهو أنه يجوز الجمع بين أمتين أختين في ملك اليمين ، فاذا وطىء إحداهما حرمت الثانية

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites argue that if obedience and disobedience are decreed by God, contradiction follows: people must accept the Messenger's ruling against an act, yet if God decreed that act they must accept it too, requiring assent to both action and abstention.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : لو كانت الطاعات والمعاصي بقضاء الله تعالى لزم التناقض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that the Messenger's decree means a legally prescribed ruling, whereas God's decree means creation and bringing into existence; these are distinct meanings and do not conflict.
rows.anchor: أن المراد من قضاء الرسول الفتوى المشروعة ، والمراد من قضاء الله التكوين والايجاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse continues the discussion of hypocrites, urging sincerity and abandonment of hypocrisy: if God had imposed killing themselves or leaving home, only a few would comply and their disbelief and defiance would be exposed; instead, out of mercy, he imposed easier duties that they should accept sincerely.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية متصلة بما تقدم من أمر المنافقين وترغيبهم في الاخلاص وترك النفاق

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر والكسائي
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Ibn Amir, and al-Kisai read the nūn of أن and wāw of أو with ḍamma, transferring the ḍamma from اقتلوا and اخرجوا.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر والكسائي : { أن اقتلوا أنفسكم أو اخرجوا من دياركم } بضم النون

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: Asim and Hamza read both vowels with kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless consonants.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة بالكسر فيهما لالتقاء الساكنين

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads the nūn with kasra and the wāw with ḍamma; al-Zajjaj knows no special reason for distinguishing them other than transmitted reading, while another scholar explains the vowels by the default kasra at two vowelless consonants and the better-sounding ḍamma on wāw.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بكسر النون وضم الواو ، وقال الزجاج : ولست أعرف لفصل أبي عمرو بين هذين الحرفين خاصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority consistently uses ḍamma on the plural pronoun wāw, as in the cited phrases from 2:16 and 2:237.
rows.anchor: واتفق الجمهور على الضم في واو الضمير نحو { اشتروا الضلالة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'they did it' refers to both killing and departure, because the two are forms of one kind of action.
rows.anchor: الكناية في قوله : { ما فعلوه } عائدة إلى القتل والخروج معا

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads قليلا in the accusative, as do the Syrian codex and the codex of Anas ibn Malik; the other readers use the nominative.
rows.anchor: واختلف القراء في قوله : { إلا قليل } فقرأ ابن عامر { قليلا } بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative treats a negative clause like an affirmative one: since the exception follows a complete sentence, it is accusative as a supplementary element.
rows.anchor: أما من نصب فقاس النفي على الاثبات ، فإن قولك : ما جاءني أحد كلام تام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative makes قليلا an appositive to the wāw in فعلوه, as an exception after a negative may follow the case of the preceding word.
rows.anchor: وأما من رفع فالسبب أنه جعله بدلا من الواو في { فعلوه }

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi calls the nominative more analogical because 'none came except Zayd' and 'only Zayd came' have the same meaning and use the nominative.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي : الرفع أقيس ، فان معنى ما أتى أحد إلا زيد ، وما أتاني الا زيد واحد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid say 'we imposed on them' refers to hypocrites: God had required Israelites to kill themselves and emigrants to leave home, so if the hypocrites faced those commands only a few would comply for show and expose their disbelief; easier duties should instead prompt sincere faith. Abu Bakr al-Asamm and al-Qaffal choose this view.
rows.anchor: قول ابن عباس ومجاهد انه عائد إلى المنافقين

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الأصم وأبو بكر القفال
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Asamm and Abu Bakr al-Qaffal select the interpretation that the pronoun refers to hypocrites.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول اختيار أبي بكر الأصم وأبي بكر القفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view takes the first pronoun generally of all people, believers and hypocrites, but the pronoun in 'if they did what they are exhorted' specifically of hypocrites; on this reading the few who would comply are believers.
rows.anchor: أن المراد لو كتب الله على الناس ما ذكر لم يفعله إلا قليل منهم

rows.speaker: ثابت بن قيس بن شماس
rows.claim: Thabit ibn Qays debated a Jew who said Moses' command to kill themselves was obeyed whereas Muhammad's command to fight is disliked; Thabit replied that he would obey Muhammad even if ordered to kill himself, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: روي أن ثابت بن قيس بن شماس ناظر يهوديا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud is also reported to have said the same thing, after which the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وروي أن ابن مسعود قال مثل ذلك ، فنزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that among his community are men whose faith is firmer in their hearts than towering mountains.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( والذي نفسي بيده إن من أمتي رجالا الايمان أثبت في قلوبهم من الجبال الرواسي )

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar swore that they would have obeyed God if ordered to kill themselves and praised God for not commanding it.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أنه قال : والله لو أمرنا ربنا بقتل أنفسنا لفعلنا

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i infers that because God did not impose such burdensome duties, he all the more did not impose what people cannot bear.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الجبائي : لما دلت هذه الآية على أنه تعالى لم يكلفهم ما يغلظ ويثقل عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author replies that the verse's rationale would also imply that God would not impose duties that disbelievers will reject and that only bring them punishment; yet God knew Abu Jahl and Abu Lahab would not believe and still imposed duties on them, so whatever answers that argument answers al-Jubba'i.
rows.anchor: ثم انه تعالى علم من أبي جهل وأبي لهب أنهم لا يؤمنون ، وأنهم لا يستفيدون من التكليف إلا العقاب الدائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'What they are exhorted by' means what they are commanded and obligated to do; it is called exhortation because God's duties include promise and warning, encouragement and deterrence, reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: أن المراد من قوله : { ولو أنهم فعلوا ما يوعظون به } أنهم لو فعلوا ما كلفوا به وأمروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised 'good' may mean the good of this world and the next, or may be comparative, meaning more beneficial and preferable; the word خير is used both ways.
rows.anchor: فيحتمل أن يكون المعنى أنه يحصل لهم خير الدنيا والآخرة ، ويحتمل أن يكون المعنى المبالغة والترجيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of 'stronger in تثبيت' is that obedience helps them persevere and continue, since an act of obedience invites similar acts and encourages persistence.
rows.anchor: أن المراد أن هذا أقرب إلى ثباتهم عليه واستمرارهم ، لأن الطاعة تدعو إلى أمثالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation is that obedience is more enduring because truth remains while falsehood passes away.
rows.anchor: أن يكون أثبت وأبقى لأنه حق والحق ثابت باق ، والباطل زائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation distinguishes the phrases: 'better' points to first acquiring good, while 'stronger in تثبيت' points to making the acquired good last.
rows.anchor: فقوله : { لكان خيرا لهم } إشارة إلى الحالة الأولى ، وقوله : { وأشد تثبيتا } إشارة إلى الحالة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincere belief and obedience would not only be better and more stable than hypocrisy but would also bring great reward and great recompense from God.
rows.anchor: كما أنه في نفسه خير فهو أيضا مستعقب الخيرات العظيمة وهو الأجر العظيم والثواب العظيم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says إذًا answers an implicit question asking what results from the good and stability: God would give them a great reward from Him, as also stated in 4:40.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : و ( إذا ) جواب لسؤال مقدر ، كأنه قيل : ماذا يكون من هذا الخير والتثبيت
